description: Pulls any element toward the pointer: translation, 3D tilt and scale on a spring, plus a soft return when the pointer moves away.
interactionNotes: As the pointer gets close, the element is pulled toward it, harder the nearer it is; at the same time it tilts slightly toward the pointer and scales up. When the pointer moves away, the spring brings it back into place instead of dropping the motion mid-way. If several magnets share one area, by default only the one closest to the pointer is pulled; turn `exclusive` off and they all build a field together. Touch screens have no pointer, so nothing moves — for that case provide `autoPreview` or a fallback animation.

props.children: The element that moves. The component has no appearance of its own; whatever you pass gets the motion.
props.padding: Pull reach from the element's edge, in pixels. Larger means it attracts from farther away.
props.magnetStrength: Pull strength; the offset is divided by this. 1 means it follows the pointer exactly, 3 means a third of the way.
props.maxOffset: Cap on the offset from the original position, in pixels. Omitting it means no cap.
props.exclusive: Only the closest magnet is pulled. Turn it off for adjacent groups so they build a field together.
props.tilt: Maximum 3D tilt toward the pointer, in degrees.
props.spring: Spring parameters; more stiffness means a faster response, more damping means a calmer return.
props.autoPreview: When there is no pointer, a phantom pointer circles the element so the pull is visible in non-interactive previews too. A real pointer always takes precedence.
props.onActiveChange: Reports entering and leaving the field.
props.wrapperClassName: Class of the outer frame — the one that sits in the layout.
props.innerClassName: Class of the inner layer — the one that moves.
props.style: Style of the outer frame (with normal HTML classes).

tips: No dependencies at all: the spring is solved on `requestAnimationFrame` and the loop puts itself to sleep once settled — zero CPU at rest.
All magnets on the page share one `pointermove` listener; dozens of magnets do not multiply the cost.
For an icon bar pass `exclusive={false}` so the whole bar bends toward the pointer, not just one icon.
It does not move on touch (there is no pointer); if you want a mobile preview, turn on `autoPreview`.
`maxOffset` is a layout safety net: without it an element near the center of the area can shift by up to half the distance.
